patch_description:
Crossover of the two 0.72-scoring seeds: I keep the low-depth, no-wrap-around
nearest-neighbor CZ chain from the "coarse-grained RY/RZ" seed (depth 29,
convergence in only 30 steps — much faster and shallower than the closed-ring
version, which needed 150 steps at depth 60), and I push the parameter-sharing
idea from the "global RY/global RZ" seed to its logical extreme: a *single*
shared trainable parameter is reused for every pre-entanglement RY gate and
every post-entanglement RZ gate on all 8 qubits. Both parents already reached
perfect train/val/test accuracy (1.00) with only 2 unique parameters per block
(14 total after repetition), so accuracy is clearly not the bottleneck —
parameter economy is what differentiates the score. By collapsing the 2
distinct per-block parameters (`p_g0/p_g1` or `ry_global/rz_global`) into a
single shared scalar `theta`, the trainable-parameter count per block is
halved (expected total n_params ≈ 7 instead of 14), which should directly
boost the parameter_efficiency term of the combined score while retaining the
shallow, fast-converging chain topology and the same expressive Y-then-Z
single-qubit rotation pattern that already generalizes perfectly. The
previous attempt to add a third parameter (`xx_ent`) increased depth,
increased convergence steps, and *hurt* the score (0.68 < 0.72), confirming
that more parameters are not helping and that shrinking the parameter count
while keeping the proven shallow chain structure is the right direction.
